notes: Account snapshot — Peregrine builds a search layer for mid-market law firms; index ~50M docs today (PDFs + contracts + precedent).
Primary goal: reduce per-query cost while improving rerank quality for long legal passages. Current stack: OpenAI embeddings + in-house cross-encoder reranker; expensive at scale.
Scaling concern: indexing 50M+ docs, batching and embedding refresh windows drive costs; they want options to quantize and run locally.
Latency SLO: 95th <= 120ms for first-pass retrieval; reranker allowed up to 400ms in some flows but overall UX target is 200ms p95.
Throughput target: sustained 200-250 qps during business hours (search-heavy spikes at 10am-12pm).
Cost target: currently ~ $0.007/query; goal <$0.003/query at 50M doc scale with caching and dedicated capacity.
Migration plan: embeddings first (canary on 1% traffic -> 10%) then reranker swap (A/B with evals + human checks). Emphasis on evals-driven gating: no regressions allowed.
Evals: automated metrics (MRR, nDCG) + sampled human judgments on legal clauses; baseline human pass-rate ~92% — new models must not drop below 90%.
Quote from Head of ML: 'We can save real dollars but only if we maintain or improve relevance — zero tolerance for regressions on precedent retrieval.'
Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance evidence, EU data residency for a subset of indexes, KMS for key control. Legal pushing for a data processing addendum before pilot expands.
Infra ask: VPC/private deployment option for on-prem-ish customers; interest in Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and private control plane.
Operational: wants rollout hooks for canary -> automatic rollback on eval regressions; ability to run parallel rerankers and shadow traffic for offline evals.
POC notes: saw a 10% latency improvement on embeddings when using Redwood-quantized variant in hosted trial; reranker still producing occasional miscues on citation normalization.
Next commercial ask: firm pricing for Dedicated 4x A100 equivalent pool and pilot discount if they commit to 12 months.
